title: Calendars: compute isOrigin from account addresses, not caller
description:
compute_is_origin (crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs:248-262) loads ParticipantIdentity with the caller's context. Since calendars -32 those are per user, so isOrigin on a shared account can depend on who created or edited the event. Neil Jenkins on jmap@ (2026-10-19, thread 'draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-33: how does the server determine isOrigin?'): 'isOrigin should not depend on the user accessing the calendar; it should be the same for everyone.' Mark told the list on 2026-11-01 it would change to an account-level set.

Done when: isOrigin uses one account-level set of addresses the account receives at (server-defined; e.g. the union of all users' ParticipantIdentity calendarAddress values, or the account's own addresses), independent of caller; a test shows two users with different identities on the same account get the same isOrigin. Keep the existing timing: compute on create and on organizerCalendarAddress change only (the ponytail comment about no recompute on identity change stays correct).
